message:
Promote measured whole-proof record af5e6e44

Set the frontier tree to the pinned base plus the exact measured patch of
whole-proof job af5e6e44-0915-4dc8-b2df-9f86ce0959ff: MEASURED_IMPROVEMENT,
FASTER_IN_EVERY_SESSION, ratio 0.8210 (95% CI 0.8127-0.8294), 17.9%
faster than the pinned prover. Patch SHA-256
0330b0792e1969e3eb4600277e416b0ac0200e8b14717c295c8cfeaca3a1d865,
83,025 bytes, 11 files, read from the evaluator's stored submission.

It supersedes the #282 frontier commit: the commitment-layer rewrite
removes the fill that #282's second change narrowed. #282's short grind
units are not included; stacking them on this frontier needs a new
measurement.

Contents and credits (write-up: bt1_b22ab32898229cf36a22d204):
- BLAKE2s compression in two 8-lane halves: omarespejel's agent Meridian,
  bt1_4cf06fb02a884724912069c1.
- Grind kernel with the round-0 prefix computed once per digest:
  Meridian, bt1_667354b3b052542baf20bcec.
- Commitment layer: tiled leaves, five fused inner layers, parallel leaf
  packing. Single-entry observation and pass merging: participant
  5992277f3a8b (odinfree), bt1_f1a94185b1a15fa340f39b91. Mechanism
  write-up: participant dbbfaeddbe89, bt1_b5c5ffbdc56ccfbeee4b0745.
- Scoped #[inline(always)] on the field operators: finding and symbol
  census by participant dbbfaeddbe89, bt1_b5c5ffbdc56ccfbeee4b0745.
- Deferred-reduction quotient accumulation: participant 5992277f3a8b
  (odinfree), bt1_4527483bd364509b01f72c85.

Review: no I/O, caching, timing or randomness; net unsafe -3, the
remaining uses are the existing uninit_vec pattern. The deferred
reduction stays below 2^64 per group of four products and folds below
2^32 before reduce_simd. stwo SIMD, lifted-Merkle, quotient and PCS
tests pass (104). The solver reports identical proof bytes and
privacy_verify acceptance on every local paired run.

Promoted at the owner's request before the 60-pair confirmation run on
another day. If that run does not confirm the result, revert this commit.

message:
Promote measured whole-proof record 2cbab192

Set the frontier tree to the pinned base plus the exact measured patch of
whole-proof job 2cbab192-d093-48ef-854c-9abecd9ec1d7: VALID_NOT_FASTER, ratio
1.0039 (95% CI 0.9997-1.0082)
against the frontier 88f22f76, so 38.1% faster than
the pinned prover. Patch SHA-256 7a405b11a0ec0cd57531dab76b10bb51e2cc25fed16f31eeb663acdf216987c3,
255,170 bytes, 58 files, read from the evaluator's stored submission.
It reports peak memory 6.88 GiB vs the frontier's 8.22 GiB in the same job (-16.2%).

On top of 88f22f76 it adds, from an agent in Omar's own session (Claude
Code, Claude Opus 5.5), one large-block cache shared by all threads, as
the global allocator. Blocks of 1 MiB and up are mapped in classes a
quarter of a power of two apart; a freed block waits in per-class slots
any thread takes from, so the temporaries one rayon worker frees no
longer sit in its glibc arena where the others cannot reuse them. Idle
memory is capped at 1 GiB, and a miss first unmaps idle blocks of other
classes down to 256 MiB. Builds on l-henri's arena finding
(bt1_313b9a8b481b747f6f63ee4e). In the same job the privacy proof
peaked at 6.88 GiB against the frontier's 8.22, at the frontier's speed.
It is bit-exact: the proofs are the unmodified prover's, byte for byte.

Review note: the allocator is a #[global_allocator] in
crates/stwo/src/prover/backend/simd/column.rs using mmap and munmap. The
file keeps its pinned unsafe count (the three tokens 88f22f76 freed
there). Over-aligned layouts (align above 4096) go to the system
allocator; a failed mmap returns null; per-class slots are single
atomics (swap to take, compare-exchange into an empty slot to keep), so
there is no list to suffer ABA.

message:

Set the frontier tree to the pinned base plus the exact measured patch of
whole-proof job d327dd5c-c28b-4393-985f-6f654f63015b: MEASURED_IMPROVEMENT, ratio
0.8213 (95% CI 0.8153-0.8273)
against the frontier 7f9715f1, so 49.1% faster than
the pinned prover. Patch SHA-256 7d89a4cb9031cfc4e67ed41ae3fdd776bb5071bff13b76d101035bf2d76b5f78,
266,158 bytes, 63 files, read from the evaluator's stored submission.
It reports peak memory 6.67 GiB vs the frontier's 6.89 GiB in the same job (-3.1%).

On top of 7f9715f1 it adds, from odinfree (Claude Code, Claude Fable 5.1),
three changes. The circuit prover keeps its preprocessed address columns
as u32 instead of usize, halving those columns, and the BLAKE G gate
drops its unpacked inputs once they are packed. In the frontier's
large-block allocator, a 2 MiB-aligned block now asks Linux for
transparent huge pages (madvise MADV_HUGEPAGE), so in madvise THP mode a
block faults once per 2 MiB instead of 512 times. In the same job the
privacy proof took 0.821 of the frontier's time (95% CI 0.815-0.827) and
peaked at 6.67 GiB against the frontier's 6.89. It is bit-exact: the
proofs are the unmodified prover's, byte for byte.

Review note: the only new unsafe call is madvise, Linux only, on blocks
the allocator itself mapped, inside the existing GlobalAlloc impl in
crates/stwo/src/prover/backend/simd/column.rs; its result is ignored, and
a refusal changes only paging. The address narrowing unwraps
u32::try_from when columns are built, so an address at or above 2^32
panics rather than wraps.

message:
Promote measured whole-proof record fccbf68b

Set the frontier tree to the pinned base plus the exact measured patch of
whole-proof job fccbf68b-8251-47a3-9228-25026e1616c1: VALID_NOT_FASTER, ratio
1.0109 (95% CI 1.0074-1.0145)
against the frontier 6e80156f, so 48.6% faster than
the pinned prover. Patch SHA-256 034f29c2eed816ab415ff30c28b54f234fe4158b7c5570097976100d0c7de567,
394,381 bytes, 70 files, read from the evaluator's stored submission.
It reports peak memory 5.87 GiB vs the frontier's 6.68 GiB in the same job (-12.1%).

On top of 6e80156f it adds, from odinfree (Codex, carrying parts of
their earlier Claude Code and Claude Fable 5.1 work), a memory
composition. A column holding only literal zeros gives its physical
pages back to Linux (madvise MADV_DONTNEED), but only after a lock-free
registry shows its exact allocation base is a live private anonymous
mapping of the frontier's large-block allocator. The allocator keeps no
idle blocks between phases, and the column pool drops its idle buffers
between the two proofs. The Cairo and circuit provers no longer store
polynomial coefficients: out-of-domain values come from a bit-reversed
prefix of each evaluation, with interpolation weights built once per
group of columns sharing a domain and sample point. FRI and Merkle
layers hash packed leaves straight from the four coordinate columns and
recompute the omitted lower layers at decommitment; logup columns are
generated in one pass, and fixed lookup-table columns are produced from
their formula instead of stored. In the same job the privacy proof
peaked at 5.87 GiB against the frontier's 6.68 (-12.1%) and took 1.011
of its time (95% CI 1.007-1.014). It is bit-exact: the proofs are the
unmodified prover's, byte for byte.

Its lead credits ryun1's lookup work, the packed FRI from workshop
threads 31 and 34, compact witness data first written with Kimi and
Codex, and the lifetime work of the research root's candidate001.

Review note: no changed file gains an unsafe token; each keeps the
frontier's count. The new page advice goes through the allocator's
existing helper, on Linux x86-64 only, over whole pages inside the
column's initialized bytes, and only when every logical word is the
literal zero MADV_DONTNEED restores. The cairo-air change factors one
affine relation for the concrete SIMD evaluator only; symbolic
evaluators, and so the verifier, see the unchanged expression.
